docs.syntax: =COUNT(range) counts numbers; =COUNTA(range) counts anything not empty
docs.explain: The count family answers three different questions that look alike. COUNT counts numbers, and it quietly skips text, blanks and logical values, so a column with six quantities and one n/a answers six. COUNTA counts every cell that is not empty, whatever it holds, so the same column answers seven because the text is still something. COUNTIF and COUNTIFS count the cells that match conditions, which is the only way to answer a question about what the values are rather than what type they are. In this drill the units column holds six numbers, one blank and one n/a, so COUNT answers six while COUNTA would answer seven; the second screen subtracts one from the other and reports the two rows where the item exists but the quantity is missing. Choosing the wrong member of the family is the classic mistake: COUNTA on a numeric column looks correct until the first text value slips into the sheet, and COUNT on a text column answers zero without warning.

errors.text: The count was combined with text where a number was expected.
